authority: R-167 v1.3 is an additive T0 topology and critical-graph route split, not a new result number. The exact all-bond kick has volume/source-uniform centered energy-graph stability and a one-layer q/p commutator recurrence. Finite-volume Lie--Trotter products therefore converge in subcritical graph powers once ordinary strong convergence and the endpoint graph bound are supplied. However, the same kick is discontinuous in the raw local basic-resolvent norm; the exact quartic onsite flow destroys the unweighted, every subcritical s<1/2, and every fixed Weyl-containing C-star-Leibniz critical seminorm that dominates a one-sided p-commutator; and the coordinate cutoff does not supply a fixed-beta half-modular-strip absolute expansion. The surviving common-dynamics obligations require a non-Leibniz analytic/Frechet or symmetric/state-weighted critical topology with a thermodynamic Cauchy theorem, or direct projected D and delta-D locality in one preregistered topology.

model.onsite_split: K_X=sum_z f_z k_z with k_z>=1+p_z^2/(2chi)+gamma|q_z|^4 and f_z/f_y in [exp(-mu),exp(mu)] on neighboring sites
model.bond_split: V_cross=-c sum_<xy>q_x.q_y and B_delta=exp(-i delta V_cross/hbar)

all_bond_centered_graph_theorem.canonical_action: B_delta^*q_xB_delta=q_x and B_delta^*p_xB_delta=p_x+delta c sum_(y~x)q_y; all cross-bond factors commute exactly.
all_bond_centered_graph_theorem.graph_bound: For 0<=s<=1/2, ||K_X^sB_(+/-delta)K_X^(-s)||<=[1+C_b(mu)|delta|]^s. A fully conjugated K^s A K^(-s) norm may use both factors and cost power 2s, whereas each orientation in N_s(C)=||CK^(-s)||+||K^(-s)C|| costs only power s.
all_bond_centered_graph_theorem.scope: This is a finite-volume form and bond-step spatial theorem. It is not onsite seminorm stability, thermodynamic Cauchy or common alpha.

finite_volume_trotter_graph_corollary.statement: The tensor-local onsite flow is an exact K_X graph isometry. If the usual finite-volume Lie--Trotter products converge strongly and have the proved uniform K_X^(1/2) product bound, interpolation first gives K_X^s graph convergence on D(K_X^(1/2-s)); uniform K_X^s T_N K_X^(-s) bounds then extend it by density to D(K_X^s), for every 0<=s<1/2.
finite_volume_trotter_graph_corollary.endpoint: The argument uses ||K^s eta||<=||eta||^(1-2s)||K^(1/2)eta||^(2s), the graph-core density of D(K^(1/2-s)) in D(K^s), and does not close s=1/2.
finite_volume_trotter_graph_corollary.scope: No volume/exhaustion limit follows from this finite-volume corollary.

raw_resolvent_point_norm_counterexample.kick: With beta_delta(A)=B_delta^*AB_delta and B_delta^*p_xB_delta=p_x+delta c q_y, beta_delta(R_x)=(i+p_x+delta c q_y)^(-1) for one neighboring component.
raw_resolvent_point_norm_counterexample.exact_norm: Because p_x and q_y strongly commute with joint spectrum R^2, the squared denominator minus the squared numerator in the resolvent-difference ratio is (1+uv)^2. Taking uv=-1 gives ||beta_delta(R_x)-R_x||=1 for every delta!=0.
raw_resolvent_point_norm_counterexample.scope: Each fixed kick can still act as a resolvent-algebra automorphism. The result rejects point-norm continuity of this subflow, not weaker graph, strict or W-star dynamics and not existence of the full Hamiltonian flow.

onsite_lipschitz_counterexample.fixture: In one component take h=p^2/(2chi)+gq^4/4 and W_a=exp(-ia p/hbar). Then [p,W_a]=0 but d/dt at t=0 of [p,alpha_t(W_a)] equals [U'(q)-U'(q-a)]W_a=g(3a q^2-3a^2q+a^3)W_a.
onsite_lipschitz_counterexample.unweighted_verdict: An operator-norm q/p Lipschitz estimate with 1+C|t| growth is impossible because the strong core derivative is an unbounded quadratic multiplier.
onsite_lipschitz_counterexample.subcritical_verdict: On translated bumps K is asymptotic to gamma q^4, so q^2K^(-s) is unbounded for every s<1/2. Both one-sided subcritical graph repairs fail this first-variation test.
onsite_lipschitz_counterexample.critical_boundary: s=1/2 survives scalar power counting but not the fixed Leibniz route. The separate critical-half theorem rejects any fixed Weyl-containing C-star-Leibniz seminorm that dominates either one-sided p-commutator and has uniform 1+C|t| onsite growth. Non-Leibniz analytic/Frechet and symmetric or state-weighted critical topologies remain open.

critical_half_leibniz_counterexample.setup: For the full one-site eight-component Q3LOCK onsite Hamiltonian h, set K=h-inf(spec h)+1, W_a=exp(-ia p_0/hbar), t_a=tau/a^2, and G=g+3lambda.
critical_half_leibniz_counterexample.force: partial_0 V4=G q_0^3-(3lambda/2)q_0^2 sum_(j~0)q_j+lambda q_0 sum_(j~0)q_j^2-(lambda/2)sum_(j~0)q_j^3.
critical_half_leibniz_counterexample.boundary_layer: Quartic coercivity and exact Heisenberg equations give ||[p_0,alpha_(t_a)(W_a)]K^(-1/2)||>=G tau a-B_tau, with B_tau finite and independent of a.
critical_half_leibniz_counterexample.leibniz_contradiction: If a fixed star-symmetric C-star-Leibniz seminorm L is finite on one nonzero W_b, dominates either one-sided critical p-commutator, and satisfies L(alpha_t(A))<=(1+C|t|)L(A), then L(W_b^n)<=nL(W_b). Taking a=nb and fixed tau>L(W_b)/(c_p G b) contradicts the boundary-layer lower bound as n tends to infinity.
critical_half_leibniz_counterexample.exact_fixture: For g=3/5, lambda=2/7, chi=7/4, G=51/35 and the backward Q3 Hamilton vector field gives Dp_0=(51/35)a^3, D^2p_0=0, D^3p_0=-(32112/8575)a^5. The scalar g=chi=1 fixture has jets a^3,0,-3a^5,0,27a^7.
critical_half_leibniz_counterexample.scope: This rejects the fixed Weyl-containing C-star-Leibniz critical route only. It does not reject non-Leibniz analytic or Frechet scales, symmetric or state-weighted topologies with energy tails, direct projected D,delta-D locality, or existence of the full dynamics.

coordinate_cutoff_half_strip_boundary.norm_c1_failure: For a smooth bounded coordinate cutoff Q_L(q), [p^2,Q_L(q)] contains p.DQ_L+DQ_L.p and is unbounded. Boundedness of the cutoff bond alone therefore does not make it norm-C1 for the quartic onsite derivation.
coordinate_cutoff_half_strip_boundary.absolute_radius: Even after an auxiliary analytic repair, a degree-z connected absolute expansion with bond norm J_L has generating parameter r=2zJ_L|Im t|/hbar. On the half modular strip |Im t|=beta hbar/2 this requires z beta J_L<1.
coordinate_cutoff_half_strip_boundary.cutoff_limit: J_L=Theta(cL^2), so no fixed beta>0 survives L to infinity through this absolute expansion. This is a proof-route boundary, not a no-go for direct projected D,delta D locality or nonabsolute resummation.

direct_relative_unitary_theorem.setup: At finite volume and fixed beta let rho=Z^(-1)exp(-beta H), K=H-W, U_H=exp(-itH/hbar), U_K=exp(-itK/hbar), and rho_t=U_K rho U_K^*. The direct theorem is first proved for bounded W. For the quadratic coordinate tail choose bounded outer cutoffs |W_M|<=|W| on the common closed forms. Their uniform infinitesimal quartic-form bound and form-core convergence imply K_M=H-W_M -> K in strong resolvent sense by Kato form convergence; Gaussian domination gives both Hilbert--Schmidt tail orientations tending to zero. Strong unitary convergence against the Hilbert--Schmidt Gibbs vectors passes the bounds to W. The entropy identity is then obtained directly from unitary entropy invariance and K-energy conservation, while its exponential bound uses the entropy variational inequality, not an unproved entropy-cutoff limit.
direct_relative_unitary_theorem.unbounded_tail_hypotheses: For each fixed finite Lambda and fixed beta: H and H-W_L share the common quartic form domain; |W_L-W_(L,M)|<=cz|Lambda|M^(-2)sum_x|q_x|^4 gives form-norm cutoff convergence; the Gibbs state has finite H-energy, phi(W_L^2)<infinity, and the displayed exponential W_L moment for the entropy bound.
direct_relative_unitary_theorem.relative_entropy: S(U_K rho U_K^*||rho)=beta[rho_t(W)-rho(W)]; for theta>beta it is at most beta/(theta-beta) log phi(exp(theta[W-phi(W)])).
direct_relative_unitary_theorem.initial_analytic_corollary: For an initial A with bounded half-modular conjugates A_-=rho^(-1/2)A rho^(1/2) and A_+=rho^(1/2)A rho^(-1/2), the direct D and D^* GNS differences are bounded by the same tail times ||A||+||A_-/+||. This needs only initial-test control, not uniform half-strip bounds for the evolved truncated multiplier.
direct_relative_unitary_theorem.scope: This closes fixed-finite-volume fixed-beta coordinate-tail approximate state invariance as L tends to infinity and a conditional initial-analytic GNS estimate. Its constants may depend on Lambda and beta. It does not provide a volume-uniform separating local analytic class, products, exhaustion, group law or common alpha.

small_direct_tail_large_multiplier_count.fixture: Let H_n=diag(0,n), rho_n proportional to exp(-beta H_n), epsilon_n=exp(-beta n/4), K_n=H_n+epsilon_n sigma_x, A=P_0, and t_n=pi hbar/sqrt(n^2+4epsilon_n^2).
small_direct_tail_large_multiplier_count.small_quantities: The perturbation W_n=-epsilon_n sigma_x and its first modular derivative tend to zero in Duhamel norm. The direct differences D_n=tau_(t_n)^(K_n)(P_0)-P_0 and [log rho_n,D_n] also tend to zero in Duhamel norm.
small_direct_tail_large_multiplier_count.failure: The off-diagonal entry of tau_(t_n)^(K_n)(P_0) makes M_0 at least asymptotic to 2exp(beta n/4)/n, and M_1 diverges faster.
small_direct_tail_large_multiplier_count.scope: Direct D,delta D convergence is strictly weaker than uniform evolved M_0,M_1. The counterexample rejects the inference, not the direct route.

representation_topology_boundary.fixture: In A=l_infinity(N), f_n=1_{k>=n} tends strong-star to zero in the faithful multiplication representation on l2(N). After adjoining a nonprincipal-ultrafilter character, the same faithful representation has f_n tending strong-star to 0 direct-sum 1.
representation_topology_boundary.consequence: Strong-star convergence in one selected faithful representation is not an abstract C-star limit and cannot by itself create a phase- and beta-independent common alpha.
representation_topology_boundary.scope: The fixed-beta modular route remains useful for a preregistered faithful W-star phase envelope and later KMS identification.

active_routes.primary_narrowed_obligation: Construct a preregistered noncollapsing non-Leibniz analytic/Frechet or symmetric/state-weighted critical topology not covered by the one-sided Leibniz no-go, prove its onsite and bond propagation plus volume/exhaustion Cauchy theorem, and identify the invariant Hamiltonian algebra.
active_routes.secondary_narrowed_obligation: Prove direct projected D and delta-D locality on a preregistered volume/source-uniform separating local test class, including product/core density, exhaustion and group law. Uniform evolved M_0,M_1 is a stronger sufficient route, not an equivalent requirement, and the failed coordinate-cutoff half-strip absolute expansion must not replace the direct theorem.
active_routes.ground_precursor: Finite-volume ground inequalities may still yield positive-energy functionals for the common local derivation on a bounded smooth core, but closability/exponentiation is required before calling them algebraic ground states or defining a GNS gap.
